clue.text: All set, having been given a nice wash, perhaps

definitions.text: All set, having been given a nice wash, perhaps

parts.words: All set, having been given a nice wash, perhaps
parts.note: pictures a little instrument you blow, freshly scrubbed and ready to go, while the phrase as a whole is an idiom for spotless or completely in order

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a laundry or bath-time remark; the answer is the everyday idiom meaning perfectly clean, with a literal glance at a washed whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spotless or entirely in order, which matches being thoroughly washed and ready.

clue.text: Unique observation about the City

indicators.note: the word for observation goes round the City's postcode letters

parts.note: espial is an old word for spying or observing
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind remark made about London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container; EC is the City of London's postcode, and espial is an old word few solvers meet outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means exceptional or particular, close in sense to unique.

clue.text: A number show enthusiasm for computer applications

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Someone with a figure in mind who loves using computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is any single numeral from 0 to 9, so it is a number.

clue.text: Isle of Man adopts language without name

indicators.note: the word for man takes in the rest, holding it inside

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a man

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside: the language wraps the letter for name

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man takes on a language that has lost its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isle of Man' looks like one place, but only 'Isle' is the definition. 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, making ERNSE, and 'adopts' signals the outer container.
explanation.definitionFit: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, so it is an isle.

clue.text: Allude to taking drug in joint

indicators.note: the verb phrase for allude to takes the drug letter inside it

parts.note: to refer to something is to allude to it
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Hinting at drug use inside a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a dive or a body part; it is the slang for a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer and joint are both slang names for a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: Irish and Chinese besieging Italian, Swiss and Iranian capitals

indicators.note: the word for Chinese surrounds the other pieces as an army encircles a town

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
Bern is the Swiss capital

indicators.note: the capital letter of the word is taken, its first letter

explanation.surface: Chinese people encircling the capitals of three other countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' works two ways across the list: Bern is the Swiss capital city, and the first letter is taken from Iranian, with I standing for Italian. HAN surrounds I+BERN+I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernian means relating to Ireland, from Hibernia, the Latin name for Ireland.

clue.text: Demon at odds with the liturgy

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds offered at the start of a race
a rite is a liturgical form of service

explanation.surface: A devil who disagrees with the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at odds with' reads as disagreeing; split it, and 'odds' gives SP, a betting abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a spirit or elf, and a demon is likewise a supernatural being.

clue.text: Torch burning amid plague and corruption gets hospital to make a commitment

indicators.note: the lit torch sits in the middle of the word for plague

parts.note: a pest is an old word for a plague
a torch is a light
a light that is burning is on
rot is decay or corruption
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: Amid pestilence and decay, someone carrying a flaming torch to a hospital makes a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' signals the container; a torch that is burning is a light that is on, and pest is an archaic word for plague.
explanation.definitionFit: To plight one's troth is an old phrase meaning to pledge faith, especially in marriage.

clue.text: Weariness of heroic canine receiving incomplete tax return

indicators.note: the dog's name takes in the other piece

parts.note: Lassie is the brave collie of films and television

indicators.note: the shortened word is read backwards
the word for tax loses its last letter

parts.note: a duty is a tax

explanation.surface: A heroic dog's fatigue after receiving part of a tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops a final letter, making DUT, and 'return' turns that to TUD before 'receiving' sets it inside; Lassie is the famous collie of film and television.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is a state of tiredness or lack of energy, a synonym of weariness.

clue.text: Force that's binding politician to student

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is wraps round the politician

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
MP is a Member of Parliament
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A force that ties a politician to a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or force someone forward, so it means to force.

clue.text: 5 dropped from mad relative's workroom

indicators.note: the numeral is taken out of the mixed-up letters
the relative's letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the word relative, taken as written, its possessive adding no letter
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A deranged relative's workshop after something has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5-down; it is the Roman numeral V. Remove V from the letters of RELATIVE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a kind of workroom.

clue.text: Charge fish with emotion

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Accuse a fish of being emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling is an emotion, the two words used interchangeably.

clue.text: Rastafarian's big number

indicators.note: read as 'has': the word has the answer within it

explanation.surface: A hit song by a Rastafarian.
explanation.definitionFit: In opera a big number is a showpiece solo song, which an aria is.

clue.text: Caustic Aussie not wholly captivated by rep

indicators.note: the shortened word is held inside the word for rep

parts.note: a rep or representative is an agent

indicators.note: the word for Aussie speech loses its last letter

parts.note: Strine is a jokey name for Australian English

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued Australian partly charmed by a sales rep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not wholly' drops a final letter, making STRIN, which 'captivated by' sets inside the rep word after its first letter; Strine is a jokey rendering of 'Australian' in an Aussie accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent can describe sharply critical remarks, just as caustic does.

clue.text: There's nothing in academic study fit for publication

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the word for academic

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
O looks like a zero, nothing
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Academic research declared worthless yet fit to print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is a verb here: to make text fit for publication by checking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading checks text for errors so it is ready to be printed, making it fit for publication.

clue.text: Unhealthy reaction to some work admitted by brother in arms

indicators.note: the unit of work is let inside the word for comrade

parts.note: an ally fights on the same side
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Someone reacting badly to tasks taken on by a fellow soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is the body's abnormal, harmful reaction to a substance.

clue.text: Trick involving simple means of ascent — climbers use it

indicators.note: the trick wraps round the slope

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
a ramp is a slope for going up

explanation.surface: A trick using a slope to get up, a tool for mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked plate fixed to a boot, used by climbers on ice.

clue.text: Many a keyboard instrument keeps time for the head man

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many

indicators.note: the instrument holds the time letter inside

parts.note: the piano is a keyboard instrument

explanation.surface: Lots of keyboards keep the beat for the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitano is Italian for captain, the chief or head man.

clue.text: Support for the devout in endless Euripides production

indicators.note: a staging of the playwright's name reworks its letters
the playwright's name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A support for worshippers inside an unending staging of a Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the S from EURIPIDES; 'production' rearranges EURIPIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a kneeling desk used for prayer, a support for the pious.

clue.text: Poet on heroin gets cable: "It's a plant!"

indicators.note: in an across answer the poet is placed after the drug letter

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
T. S. Eliot was a poet
a rope is a cable

explanation.surface: A drug-addled poet receives a telegram announcing a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cable' suggests a telegram; it is a thick rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a garden plant with fragrant purple flowers.

clue.text: Where art is visible to the blind?

definitions.text: Where art is visible to the blind?

parts.words: Where art is visible to the blind?
parts.note: the blind is a window shutter of slats, not sightless people, and the same word names a famous Paris gallery

explanation.walkthrough: 'the blind' seems to mean people who cannot see; it is a slatted window blind, which shares its name with the Paris art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris museum houses great art, and a louvre is a slatted shutter.

clue.text: Eliminate clods with intellectual challenge

definitions.meaning: to sift soil through a coarse sieve, removing lumps

explanation.walkthrough: A riddle is also a coarse garden sieve, so to riddle soil is to sift the clods out.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to sieve soil; as a noun, a brain-teaser.

clue.text: Where to put up with provocative remarks

explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented lodgings; digs are also sly jabs at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodgings are informally called digs, and pointed jibes are digs too.

clue.text: Smell an anthropoid

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Sniff out an ape-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropoid means resembling a human, and a human is a member of mankind.

clue.text: Encouraged Murphy to take back stray

indicators.note: the potato word takes the turned piece inside

parts.note: murphy is slang for a potato, as is spud

indicators.note: the word for stray is read backwards

parts.note: to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Someone named Murphy urged to take back a stray animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' looks like a surname; it is old slang for a potato. 'back' turns ERR to RRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spurred is to be urged on or encouraged.

clue.text: Origins of terrific hubbub below and terrific hubbub above

indicators.note: the first letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: under means beneath or below

explanation.surface: The beginnings of a din down below and a great racket overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is a tremendous noise from the sky overhead, so a terrific hubbub above.

clue.text: King occupying throne with a grub

indicators.note: the king letter sits inside the word for throne

parts.note: the throne is jokey slang for a toilet, a lav
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king sitting on his throne with a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' looks royal but means a toilet, LAV in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young form of an insect, also called a grub.

clue.text: Feature with 9 metal components

indicators.note: the letters are treated as parts to be put together in a new order

parts.note: nine spelled out as a word

explanation.surface: A characteristic with nine metal parts.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a reference to 9-across; it is the number nine, spelled NINE and mixed with METAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a distinctive feature, especially of the face.
